target_statement: Every finite group G contains a subgroup H generated by at most two elements such that exp(H)=exp(G).

source_clauses.text: Is it true that any finite group contains a 2-generated subgroup with the same exponent?
An affirmative answer is known for soluble groups.
It is also known that any finite group contains a 3-generated subgroup with the same exponent.

constraints.statement: The assertion quantifies over every finite group G; a counterexample is one finite G for which no eligible subgroup exists.
H is a subgroup of G; it is not required to be proper.
There exist x,y in G such that H=<x,y>; equivalently H can be generated by at most two elements.
The group exponents are exactly equal: exp(H)=exp(G), where exponent is the least common multiple of all element orders.
For every finite G, at least one subgroup H satisfying all preceding rows exists.

excluded_scopes: The already-known assertion restricted to soluble groups
The weaker statement with a 3-generated subgroup
Equality only of maximum element order rather than equality of group exponents
A bounded catalogue pass presented as a proof of the universal assertion

success_criteria.proof: Prove for every finite group G that some subgroup generated by at most two elements has exponent exactly exp(G).
success_criteria.counterexample: Give one explicit finite group G and prove exhaustively that exp(<x,y>) is strictly smaller than exp(G) for every x,y in G.
partial_progress: A complete reproducible exclusion of counterexamples in a precisely bounded nonsoluble family.
A proved reduction to almost simple groups, chief factors, or another explicitly defined residual family.
success_criteria.certificate: A proof, or a reconstructible finite group together with exact exponent computation and a complete pair-orbit or all-pairs certificate covering every 2-generated subgroup.

truth_likelihood.rationale: The theorem is known for all soluble groups and with three generators in general, which favors truth; the counterexample direction is still the cheapest first reconnaissance because one finite nonsoluble witness would settle the question.

priority.rationale: The target has a compact finite counterexample certificate and admits complete bounded searches with exact exponent checks, while structural near misses can expose a residual almost-simple obstruction.

MONOLITHIC-SOCLE-GATE stopped after three active minutes: direct indecomposability plus strict exponent drop in every proper subgroup and nontrivial proper quotient does not force a unique minimal normal subgroup. The order-30 dihedral group with rotation order 15 is an explicit soluble obstruction to that inference, not a counterexample to the target.

THREE-PAIR-DEFECT-HYPERGRAPH used six active minutes. It derives that a counterexample has at least three exponent primes; in the exactly-three-prime case, maximal pure prime-power elements generate the least counterexample and the three pair defects are the three distinct omitted primes. For an abelian minimal normal p-layer, quotient p-exponent drops exactly one level and the split case has a nonzero norm condition. General edge labels are not Nielsen-invariant, so unrestricted defect coloring is exhausted. These subclaims await validation.

THREE-PRIME-ABELIAN-CHIEF-NORM used seven active minutes. It proposes that a chief p-layer raising p^(a-1) to p^a forces a full Jordan block of length p^(a-1), but an explicit soluble split action with exponent 900 satisfies the candidate local rows while the order-9 element has no single partner carrying the complementary order-4 and order-25 powers. The pattern refutes only the norm implication; every structural claim and the presented group require fresh validation.

The universal assignment remains open.

Truth estimate 0.68 and the exhausted counterexample-local patterns justify switching to a clean proof direction. TWO-MINIMAL-NORMAL-SUBDIRECT-PAIRING tests whether distinct minimal normals permit compatible two-generator full-exponent pairs from the two proper quotients, potentially forcing a least counterexample to be monolithic under the full nonsoluble/d(G)=3 hypotheses.

The subdirect-pairing pass used nine active minutes and gives an exact candidate reduction: for G=A x_C B, a two-generator subgroup of exponent exp(G)=lcm(exp(A),exp(B)) exists exactly when one Nielsen orbit in Hom(F_2,C) supports attainable projected exponents r and s with lcm(r,s)=exp(G). Minimality makes the two separate full-factor orbit sets nonempty but does not force their intersection. Route this criterion to fresh independent validation; it is a structural partial only and does not prove monolithicity or answer the universal scope.

Validator upholds the fibre-product, exponent-lcm, arbitrary-F_2-map, and common-precomposition-orbit criterion, repairing only the shorthand that intersection of full-factor witness sets is sufficient but not necessary. The common base map may be required epimorphic in a successful profile, while factor maps need not be. Resume on BASE-PREIMAGE-PRIME-COVER: pull back a minimality-supplied two-generated full-exponent subgroup of C and test whether proper preimage exponent drops force a common prime-profile contradiction.

BASE-PREIMAGE-PRIME-COVER used nine active minutes, bringing the ledger to 74. It proposes a fixed extension-created prime-defect set for every proper two-generated full-exponent base subgroup, exact top-lift supports whose arbitrary transversals generate the common quotient, and a dichotomy between d(C)=3 base-rank obstruction and d(C)<=2 cross-intersecting epimorphic loss profiles. This is a candidate conditional partial only; route every implication to fresh validation before reuse.
